clue.text: Tap-dances round piles of dried grass

indicators.note: round says the dances are placed around the tap, enclosing it

parts.note: the hay is an old country dance, so dances are hays
a cock is a tap or valve, as in stopcock

explanation.surface: Someone tap-dancing around heaps of hay in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'Tap-dances' disguises two separate words; 'round' is the container signal, and HAY here is the old country dance, not dried grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Haycocks are small conical heaps in which hay is left to dry in the field.

clue.text: False belief I initially renounced for a reference

indicators.note: says the I at the start is given up in favour of the letter a

parts.note: an illusion is a mistaken belief

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a misconception and turns to a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion is an indirect mention or reference to something.

clue.text: Thief takes oath, wrongly put inside

indicators.note: inside says the rearranged word goes within the oath

parts.note: a curse is a swear word or oath

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of put are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A thief swears after being wrongly jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' gives TPU; 'takes' and 'put inside' both look like a prison story, but only 'inside' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutpurse is an old word for a pickpocket, who once cut purses from belts.

clue.text: Name American who's fighting with Rugby League hooker

parts.note: to call is to name
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A named American soldier plays alongside a rugby league hooker.
explanation.walkthrough: A hooker is a rugby forward position, but here it means a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooker is slang for a prostitute, who may be booked by telephone.

clue.text: Two fellows with right, say, to be over-formal?

parts.note: Stan is a man's name
Don is a second man's name
right said aloud is rite, which is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Two men claim the right to act stiffly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right, say' asks for a word that sounds like right, rite, then for its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist on the proper etiquette and formalities is the meaning of this idiom.

clue.text: They carry diseases caught in club upriver

indicators.note: in says the cricket letter goes inside the club

parts.note: a bat is a club for striking a ball
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the Aire is a Yorkshire river; going up it in a down clue reads its name from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Germs picked up in a riverside club upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upriver' looks like a place, but it gives the river Aire written upwards, ERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Some bacteria are germs that cause and spread infection.

clue.text: Guides — type going over Northern Ireland

indicators.note: in a down clue going over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: cicero is a unit of type size in printing

explanation.surface: Tour guides of one kind travel across to Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicerones are guides who show sightseers around, named after the eloquent orator.

clue.text: Men had to manoeuvre to obtain noble rank

indicators.note: to manoeuvre is to move things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men had to jockey for position to gain a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A thanedom is the rank and lands of a thane, an Anglo-Saxon nobleman.

clue.text: Comrade has to put on a shiny coat, not new

indicators.note: put on says the first piece is placed in front of the second

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not says a letter standing for new is removed from the coat

parts.note: varnish is a glossy coating

explanation.surface: A comrade has to apply a gloss coat to something that is no longer new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops the N, leaving VARISH; 'put on' reads as donning a coat but signals placing in front. The answer is a borrowing from Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: Tovarish is the Russian word for a fellow communist, used for a comrade.

clue.text: Loud bunch damage a number of boats

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud
a lot is a group or bunch
ill is harm or damage, as in 'do no ill'

explanation.surface: A noisy gang vandalises several boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet, a group of ships sailing together.

clue.text: Like Newcastle, prime minister associated with English navy

parts.note: Lord North was British prime minister during the American War of Independence
RN stands for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A political note on a prime minister's links with Newcastle and the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWCASTLE is a city in the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle upon Tyne lies in the north of England, so it is a city of that region.

clue.text: Relieved a French artist's received American backing

indicators.note: backing says the artist piece with its insertion is read from right to left
received says the artist's name takes the American abbreviation inside it

parts.note: Degas is the French Impressionist painter, plus 's

explanation.surface: A French painter, sponsored by Americans, felt relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received' puts US inside DEGAS'S, giving DEGAUSS; 'backing' turns that to SSUAGED, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to ease or soothe, so relieved pain has been assuaged.

clue.text: Position of shepherd reveals geological feature

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a shepherd watches over the sheepfold, so his place is above the fold
a fold in rock strata that has been pushed over beyond the vertical

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into OVER and FOLD, a sheep pen.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology an overturned fold, whose limbs both dip the same way, is given this name.

clue.text: Thrown in cell, stimulate cerebral activity

indicators.note: thrown, as in thrown into disorder, says the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone flung into a prison cell has to keep their mind busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown' looks like a prisoner's fate but is the signal to rearrange INCELLSTIMULATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Intellectualism is devotion to the exercise of the intellect and reason.

clue.text: European is headmaster in Asian country

indicators.note: in says the two pieces go inside the country

parts.note: Iran is a country in Asia
taken as written
HM is short for headmaster

explanation.surface: A European is head of a school in an Asian land.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Ireland is one kind of European.

clue.text: Coolness of note I had written in sympathy

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: written in says the contraction goes inside the word for sympathy

parts.note: pity is sympathy
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A lukewarm note written in sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepidity is lukewarmness, a lack of warmth or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Luxurious quality — with soft top, likewise

definitions.text: Luxurious quality — with soft top, likewise

parts.words: Luxurious quality — with soft top, likewise
parts.note: a word for luxuriance which, with p for soft placed on top, makes another word for luxuriousness

explanation.surface: A soft-topped item is just as luxurious.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano, soft) added in front gives PLUSHNESS, which also means luxurious quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Lushness is richness and abundance, the quality of being luxuriant.

clue.text: Not a favourite sort of grape

definitions.meaning: in tennis, a player not ranked among the favourites in the draw

explanation.definitionFit: Unseeded means both unranked in a tournament and lacking pips, as a grape bred without them.

clue.text: At the seaside? Sounds like a misprint

indicators.note: sounds like says the word for a misprint is heard, not read

parts.note: a literal is a printing error of a single letter

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker wonders whether a seaside sign contains a typo.
explanation.definitionFit: Littoral means relating to the shore, the coastal zone by the sea.

clue.text: In second half of case, cite old sectarian

indicators.note: in says the word for cite sits inside the pair of letters
second half of takes the last two of the four letters of case

parts.note: to adduce is to cite as evidence

explanation.surface: In the latter part of a court case, an old religious partisan is cited.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sadducees were a Jewish sect of the Second Temple period, rivals of the Pharisees.

clue.text: Fraud quietly entering island with maximum amount of gold

indicators.note: entering says the soft musical letter goes into the word for the largest amount

parts.note: the most is the greatest amount
P, piano, means quietly in music
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A con artist sneaks onto an island carrying all the gold he can.
explanation.definitionFit: An impostor deceives others by pretending to be someone else, a kind of cheat.

clue.text: Smooth current observed late in the day

parts.note: even means level or smooth
a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: Calm water was seen running in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the close of the day.

clue.text: Cutting-edge academic is pursuing pleasure

indicators.note: cutting says the academic piece slices into the word for edge

parts.note: a hem is the edge of a garment
a don is a university teacher
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leading-edge scholar is chasing enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting-edge' reads as praise for the academic; the hyphen hides that 'Cutting' is a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the doctrine or practice of living for gratification and enjoyment.

clue.text: Stubbornness of odd bod replacing head of church office

indicators.note: odd says the letters of bod are taken in a strange order
replacing head of says the first letter of the office is swapped for the other piece

parts.note: a curacy is the office of a curate in the church

explanation.surface: A peculiar character takes over from the head of a church office, showing obstinacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' gives OBD, and 'odd bod' looks like a description of an eccentric person rather than an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Obduracy is hard-hearted obstinacy, refusal to change one's mind.

clue.text: Painting finally done by Welsh girl? Well, sort of

parts.note: painting is a form of art

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word done

parts.note: Sian is a common Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman finishes a painting, more or less satisfactorily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a mild interjection; it is the noun, a water well.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well taps water under pressure so that it rises by itself.

clue.text: Alpine vocalist's greeting to famous countertenor

indicators.note: to says the greeting is joined in front of the singer's name

parts.note: yo is an informal greeting
Alfred Deller was the celebrated English countertenor

explanation.surface: A Swiss singer calls out hello to a renowned countertenor.
explanation.definitionFit: A yodeller sings with rapid switches into falsetto, a style of the Swiss and Austrian mountains.
